text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a non-review research study that explicitly implements a national-scale (entire Netherlands) GIS-based land use model—Land Use Scanner—to simulate future residential and other land use patterns under three distinct quantitative scenarios (Divided Europe, European Co-ordination, Global Competition). The primary objective is to predict and analyze spatially explicit LULC changes up to 2020, with mapped outputs (e.g., Figures 2–4). The modeling includes suitability analysis calibrated on historical data (1980–1995), dynamic allocation across 193,399 grid cells, and integration of policy constraints. Although environmental impacts are assessed, LULC prediction is the central methodological and analytical focus. The study meets all core inclusion criteria: national-scale implementation, primary focus on LULC simulation, ≥2 future scenarios with quantitative comparison, spatially explicit modeling, and mapped LULC projections. It does not meet any exclusion criteria.)
